lines.text: Lesson twenty-three: the full scalping decision lifecycle, from chart to journal.
This is the capstone: T14 to T22, used together on one fictional chart.
Eight steps, in the same order every time, from choosing a coin to writing a journal.
It's an educational simulation, in demo mode. No real money, no real orders.
And we score the process, not the profit.
Step one: choose a coin. In this simulation, the coins and all prices are made up.
Liquidity means how easily you can buy or sell without moving the price much.
BTC/USDT has many traders and a tiny spread. XYZ/USDT is thin: a 1% spread.
Thin coins slip more. So we pick BTC/USDT, on a 1,000 USDT demo account.
Step two: context. First the 5-minute chart, for the bigger picture of the last hour.
Higher highs and higher lows. So on 5 minutes, the trend leans up. Trends can still end.
Now zoom into the last 15 minutes on the 1-minute chart. Same prices, more detail.
The 1-minute chart is noisier: a run up, then a pull-back. Use it for detail, not direction.
Step three: range and levels. Over 15 minutes, the high was 60,650 and the low 59,850.
That's a range of 800 USDT, about 1.3% of the price.
Twice, price dipped into 59,850 to 59,950 and bounced. That's our support zone.
Resistance sits near the top, 60,550 to 60,650. Price is now 60,000, just above support.
Step four: write down what you're unsure about. Beginners often skip this step.
What I lean towards: a bounce up from support, because the 5-minute trend is up.
What argues against it: support was already tested twice, and it could break.
What would prove me wrong: a fall below 59,700. Confidence: medium, not certain.
Step five: costs and risk, before any button. Example numbers only, not a recommendation.
Entry near 60,000. Stop at 59,700, just under support. That's 300 USDT away: 0.5%.
Example budget: 6 USDT. Fees at 0.05% each way take about 1, leaving 5 for the price move.
5 divided by 0.5% gives a notional of about 1,000 USDT. No leverage needed.
Stop hit: about −6 USDT with fees. Target 60,600 hit: +10 minus fees, about +9 USDT.
Step six: decide. DEMO BUY, DEMO SELL or NO_TRADE. All three are allowed.
Whatever you choose, write one or two lines of why. A direction alone is not a reason.
Here: trend up, a bounce at support, and a planned loss of about 6 USDT, inside the budget.
So this learner picks DEMO BUY, with the stop and target set at the same time.
Step seven: monitor and exit. From here, price could go up, sideways or down.
Nobody knows which path will come. That's why the stop and target were set first.
Now the replay. Price rises to 60,400. Tempting to dream, but the plan stays the same.
Then it turns, breaks support, and hits the stop. The fill is 59,680: 20 USDT of slippage.
The exit happens as planned, about eight minutes in. No moving the stop, no adding more.
Step eight: the journal. Write what you planned, what happened, and what you learned.
Price result: −5.33 USDT. Fees: −1.00. Net: −6.33 USDT, close to the plan.
Did we follow the plan? Yes: size, stop and exit all as written. Process score: 8 of 8.
A good process can still lose. Judge decisions by the process, not by one outcome.
Now the other route. Another learner saw the same chart and the same numbers.
Their notes: support tested twice, weak volume on the bounce, not confident. So: NO_TRADE.
Result: 0 USDT, no fees, and a journal entry. Process: complete. That's a success too.
Not because of how the replay ended. They decided before knowing, with a clear reason.
Three common mistakes. First: moving the stop further away as price gets close.
That turns a planned 6 USDT loss into about 11. Keep the stop where the plan put it.
Second: doubling the size to win a loss back. That doubles the risk too. Take a break first.
Third: judging only by profit. Judge the process, because good process can still lose.
Your turn. The stop must go at 59,400: 1% away. The budget for the move is still 5 USDT.
About what notional fits? Pause if you need more time.
B, about 500 USDT. 5 divided by 1% is 500. A wider stop means a smaller position.
A is tempting, but 1,000 USDT with a 1% stop risks 10 USDT, double the budget.
Honest limits. A simulation is not the market: real fills can slip more, and real money feels different.
Even a careful plan loses often. Never trade money you can't afford to lose.
This plan used no leverage. More leverage makes losses bigger and can lead to liquidation.
Everything here is fictional and educational, not advice. NO_TRADE is always allowed.
Recap. One: eight steps, in order, from choosing a coin to writing the journal.
Two: your size comes from the risk budget and the stop distance, before deciding.
Three: judge the process, not one outcome. NO_TRADE can be a full success.
Check yourself: you followed the plan and still lost. Bad decision?
Not necessarily. Check the process first.
Next up: Checkpoint B, a review of T14 to T23. Well done for reaching the end of the lessons!
